svg.aria-label: A few commands. No settings window.. /model [filter]: Choose a model from OMP's catalogue, across providers, without starting a new conversation /login: Follow the harness's own sign-in steps inside the box, browser sign-in or key entry /usage: See the harness's usage reports and reset times; providers without a report are marked /backup [filter]: Set an ordered fallback list: Enter adds or removes a model, Esc saves it /harness: See which Oh-my-pi the box runs, the built-in one or your own, and switch between them /update: Move the built-in Oh-my-pi to the newest version the repository's harness check has passed, and say when a newer Null is out and what gets it /attach [path]: Hand the agent a file with the next message: choose it from a list of your folders inside the box, or give its path. The plus at the end of the row does the same /history [words]: List the earlier conversations, the box's own and the terminal's, and open one again. Typing narrows the list by title and folder, then adds the conversations in which those words were said. Tab sorts it by folder. On a row, the pencil renames and the x moves the conversation to the Trash. Conversations that are working, asking or not yet looked at come first, under "now". The button after the plus opens the same list /rename <title>: Give the open conversation a title of your own. In /history, Command+R does it for the chosen row, and Command+Delete moves that row to the Trash /pet: Show the pet beside the box, or put it away /computer: See whether the agent may see the screen and work the apps on this Mac, and switch it. While it is on, the list also says how the two permissions macOS wants for it stand, and Enter on a missing one asks macOS for it /folder [path]: Start a new conversation in a folder of your choosing, where the agent has that project's files and instructions: pick one that conversations already work in, walk to another, or give its path. The box says where each time such a conversation comes to the front /new: Start a fresh conversation on the last selected model, in the box's own folder. A conversation that is working goes on; at most four work at once /quit: Quit and clear the saved conversation pointer. With conversations still working it says how many first, and quits when asked again /<name>: OMP's own commands and the skills it finds, your Playbook among them, are listed under the box's own, and one is carried out there when you type it by the name the list shows, arguments and all A lone /word is not sent to the agent as a message: it opens the list, which holds both the box's own commands and the ones the harness says it can carry out, each with a few words. A name only the harness knows is sent as the harness spells it, so a skill of yours is typed by the name you know it by. A name neither has is not sent at all. Other messages go through normally. A listed model is not a guarantee that your account can use it: providers with reported limits exhausted are dimmed but stay selectable, and a model change waits until the current reply is stopped or finished.

g.text: A few commands. No settings window.
/model [filter]
Choose a model from OMP's catalogue, across providers, without starting a new
conversation
/login
Follow the harness's own sign-in steps inside the box, browser sign-in or key
entry
/usage
See the harness's usage reports and reset times; providers without a report are
marked
/backup [filter]
Set an ordered fallback list: Enter adds or removes a model, Esc saves it
/harness
See which Oh-my-pi the box runs, the built-in one or your own, and switch between
them
/update
Move the built-in Oh-my-pi to the newest version the repository's harness check
has passed, and say when a newer Null is out and what gets it
/attach [path]
Hand the agent a file with the next message: choose it from a list of your
folders inside the box, or give its path. The plus at the end of the row does the
same
/history [words]
List the earlier conversations, the box's own and the terminal's, and open one
again. Typing narrows the list by title and folder, then adds the conversations
in which those words were said. Tab sorts it by folder. On a row, the pencil
renames and the x moves the conversation to the Trash. Conversations that are
working, asking or not yet looked at come first, under "now". The button after
the plus opens the same list
/rename <title>
Give the open conversation a title of your own. In /history, Command+R does it
for the chosen row, and Command+Delete moves that row to the Trash
/pet
Show the pet beside the box, or put it away
/computer
See whether the agent may see the screen and work the apps on this Mac, and
switch it. While it is on, the list also says how the two permissions macOS wants
for it stand, and Enter on a missing one asks macOS for it
/folder [path]
Start a new conversation in a folder of your choosing, where the agent has that
project's files and instructions: pick one that conversations already work in,
walk to another, or give its path. The box says where each time such a
conversation comes to the front
/new
Start a fresh conversation on the last selected model, in the box's own folder. A
conversation that is working goes on; at most four work at once
/quit
Quit and clear the saved conversation pointer. With conversations still working
it says how many first, and quits when asked again
/<name>
OMP's own commands and the skills it finds, your Playbook among them, are listed
under the box's own, and one is carried out there when you type it by the name
the list shows, arguments and all
A lone /word is not sent to the agent as a message: it opens the list, which holds both the box's
own commands and the ones the harness says it can carry out, each with a few words. A name only the
harness knows is sent as the harness spells it, so a skill of yours is typed by the name you know
it by. A name neither has is not sent at all. Other messages go through normally. A listed model is
not a guarantee that your account can use it: providers with reported limits exhausted are dimmed
but stay selectable, and a model change waits until the current reply is stopped or finished.
